text:
Rae (SRE): Alert: embedding-service in eu-west-1 showing p99 latencies > 2s since ~09:00 UTC and increased timeouts to downstream customers. Connecting traces now.

CacheBot: [ALERT] Redis eviction count spike on redis-cluster-euwest (cache-redis). Evictions per sec = 120.

Nina (Support): Got multiple customer reports about slow onboarding flows that call embeddings sync. Raising priority.

Rae (SRE): Traces show hot key patterns hitting a single redis shard. Memory pressure triggered aggressive evictions; cache misses cascade to embedding model, causing extra model calls and queueing.

Elena (Eng): Did we recently change the cache TTL or prefixing? I deployed a change yesterday that added user-email as part of the cache key for embeddings (ship-embed-keys PR). Could create cardinality spike.

Kai (Infra): I see the redis cluster OOM events at 08:57. Pod restarts observed. Failingover around 09:05.

Rae (SRE): Immediate mitigation: 1) roll back key-change (revert commit a9d4c), 2) increase redis memory limit on affected shard, 3) add temporary read-through cache bypass for heavy paths to reduce model load. Executed commands:
```
kubectl -n cache rollout undo deployment cache-redis --to-revision=12
kubectl -n cache patch statefulset redis-shard-3 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"redis","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"8Gi"}}}]}}}}'
```

Nina (Support): Posting status update to customers: "We are experiencing elevated latencies for embeddings in eu-west-1. Our team has identified a cache key regression and applied mitigations. We will update in 30 minutes."

StatusPage Bot: Posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2024-043 1: Partial service degradation for embeddings in eu-west-1.

Elena (Eng): Rollback confirmed. Reverting key change reduced unique key cardinality by ~92% per metrics. Redis eviction rate dropped within 7 minutes.

Kai (Infra): After scale and rollback, p95/p99 latencies dropping. Still monitoring for late queues. I've pinned an extra redis replica to shard-3 for 2 hours to prevent flapping.

Rae (SRE): Current status: mitigated. Latencies near normal, no active customer-facing errors. Keeping incident channel open for monitoring window.

Elena (Eng): Root cause (prelim): deployment changed embedding cache key to include high-cardinality identifier (email) causing cache explosion and evictions. Follow-ups: 1) postmortem w/ action items, 2) stricter review checklist for cache-key changes, 3) an alert for sustained eviction spikes and hot-shard detection, 4) automated canary to measure key cardinality after deploy.

Nina (Support): Comms draft ready in incident doc: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2024-043/comms.md — please review before public update.

Rae (SRE): Marking incident as resolved for now. We'll keep an eye for 1 hour and then close. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
